players.name: Gary Neville
players.note: Peak Neville: positionally excellent and an intelligent defender, never an athletic or attacking outlier. Good rather than elite.

players.name: David Beckham
players.note: Runner-up for the Ballon d’Or; the best right-sided midfielder in the world that season. Elite delivery and range of passing, ordinary one-v-one.

players.name: Roy Keane
players.note: The reinvention as a deeper, controlling midfielder: the treble season and the Juventus semi-final are the evidence.

players.name: Dwight Yorke
players.note: The best season of his career: 18 league goals in a treble side, and among the most complete forwards in Europe that year.

players.name: Jaap Stam
players.note: World class: pace, strength and reading combined, and in 1998/99 in the conversation for the best centre-back in Europe. Rated above Adams (88) and just under Ferdinand 2007/08 (91).

players.name: Ryan Giggs
players.note: At his peak: among the best wide players in Europe in the treble season, even with the appearance total held down by hamstrings.

players.name: Ronny Johnsen
players.note: Excellent alongside Stam in the treble season; a genuinely good centre-half whose career was cut short by injury rather than a limit of ability.

players.name: Wes Brown
players.note: Broke into a treble-winning defence at 18; rated as the promising teenager he was, not the England international he became.

players.name: Henning Berg
players.note: A rotation option at United rather than a first choice, and injured for much of the treble season.

players.name: Ole Gunnar Solskjær
players.note: Twelve league goals from 859 minutes, mostly from the bench. Rated on finishing ability, not on the limited starting role behind Yorke and Cole.

players.name: Teddy Sheringham
players.note: A poor, peripheral first season at United - seven starts and visibly short of confidence.
